> "this chapter provides more general guidance on how to develop secure applications and how to write secure code correctly"
> 
> If to read it really literally, we don't describe HOW to develop or HOW to write, we have requirements for verifying the result. "HOW TO" describes the process to achieve that and that is out of scope.

I would agree that most developer guidance on how to develop secure applications and how to write secure code correctly has been removed. This standard is not very actionable by developers anymore. But I do admit it's a great deal more focused on and better for security testers.

> "this chapter provides more general guidance on how to develop secure applications and how to write secure code correctly"
> 
> If to read it really literally, we don't describe HOW to develop or HOW to write, we have requirements for verifying the result. "HOW TO" describes the process to achieve that and that is out of scope.

I would agree that most developer guidance on how to develop secure applications and how to write secure code correctly has been removed.

Elar, I was just trying to echo a comment you made earlier. 

> If to read it really literally, we don't describe HOW to develop or HOW to write, we have requirements for verifying the result. "HOW TO" describes the process to achieve that and that is out of scope.

I feel the direction of ASVS is a lot more actionable for testers and less so for developers. So many of the code quality and engineering requirements have gone away to recommendations section. This is not an attack on you or Josh -  its just my perspective. When working with developers, which is my life's work, we need to be very specific at the code level, and most of ASVS has removed my and others earlier attempts to add that in. What we have now is more of a testing standard, less of a developer one. And that is not all an attack on you, it's a concern and perspective from me, echoed from your own comments.

Did I miss something? I am open to you feedback on this.
